decision: As SysML 8.2.2.12 states it: `~` followed by `~[QualifiedName]`. Note 2 of the clause says that notation parses an ordinary QualifiedName from the text and changes only how it resolves: to the conjugated port definition named `'~C'` inside `A::B::C`. So syntactically it is `~` then a QualifiedName. The Xtext writes `conjugatedPortDefinition = [SysML::ConjugatedPortDefinition | ConjugatedQualifiedName]`, where its ConjugatedQualifiedName rule is `'~' QualifiedName`: the same tokens. The clause names the property `originalPortDefinition` and the Xtext `conjugatedPortDefinition`; a property name consumes no tokens.

evidence.note: ConjugatedPortTyping : ConjugatedPortTyping = '~' originalPortDefinition = ~[QualifiedName], with Note 2 defining ~[QualifiedName] as a QualifiedName parsed normally and resolved to the conjugated definition
ConjugatedPortTyping: conjugatedPortDefinition = [SysML::ConjugatedPortDefinition | ConjugatedQualifiedName], with ConjugatedQualifiedName: '~' QualifiedName (SysML.xtext line 976). The same tokens.

notes: re-scoped (ADR-0015): only the sysml grammar reaches this production, so its work now lives in ConjugatedPortTyping@sysml
